Each truncated Ck norm contributes a symmetric triangle-inequality metric term; the weighted sum separates backgrounds.
A Cauchy sequence for b is Cauchy in every Ck norm, with consistent limits defining a smooth form.
Nonnegative area is retained by C0 convergence, and finite-sum plus tail control identifies the C-infinity topology.
Polar curvature classifies models for arbitrary smooth nonnegative-area curve backgrounds, including the zero-area singleton.
The mass constraint on a polar measure is closed under smooth background and total-variation measure convergence.
Positivity survives total variation and polar support survives through the countable union of the actual measure carriers.
The product metric separates model/background pairs and restricts to the established complete polar metric on each fiber.
Completeness of finite signed measures and of the background space supplies a realizable limiting pair.
Ideal projection is atomic extraction and its coordinatewise contraction makes the full pair map1-Lipschitz.
Atomic measures are closed because their total-variation limit is carried by the countable union of atom sets, not their potentially uncountable topological supports.
Diffuse and signed atomic parts are mutually singular; the distance decomposition remains valid when the target background differs.
The unique nearest ideal pair has the identical background and exactly the original atomic measure, satisfying its area bound.
Finite rational atomic approximations can be chosen strictly below positive area, including for an atomic measure saturating that area.
Smooth-gauge curve classification gives analytic ordinary models with those actual rational pole coefficients.
At zero area, adding j-inverse eta yields an admissible positive-area background with zero polar measure and positive residual mass.
Those zero-polar models are bounded by the curve classification, so they have trivial analytic singularities.
Every analytic model is its ideal projection, and closedness gives the converse analytic-closure inclusion.
Positive limiting area permits eventual positive area ratios tending to one; the displayed total-variation rescaling error tends to zero.
The existing arbitrary-background continuity theorem then gives L1 and capacity convergence of normalized potentials.
At zero limiting area, uniform convergence of the smooth backgrounds satisfies the full nonnegative-area collapse theorem.
Completeness explicitly uses smooth background convergence; uniform-norm completeness of the smooth-form domain is not asserted.
The fixed positive-area fiber has the established positive-volume topology while changing its boundary Cauchy behavior.
Smooth gauge transport preserves polar coordinates and area, and translation leaves all background differences and b unchanged.
The gauge inverse and composition laws follow from the exact polar-coordinate representation, and analytic types are preserved.
Scaling ordinary-envelope competitors gives the normalized model lambda p and scales its polar measure by lambda.
The truncated-norm inequalities hold both above and below1, and combine with exact variation-norm scaling to give the stated bi-Lipschitz bounds.
Both maps commute with atomic extraction; analytic preservation is not asserted for irrational scaling.
The general higher-dimensional, zero-volume and non-BMP problem remains open; no novelty or independent external-proof certification is claimed.
